source: The Namibian - No cholera cases recorded in over a decade (11 March 2025)
processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 2015-01-01..2018-01-21. Source states: 'Namibia has not recorded any cholera cases in the past 10 years.'. Evidence type: Inferred_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: operational. T1 ADJUDICATION (Agent 3, 2026-09-30): replaces the pre-2018 part of retracted AI 7 (2015-01-01..2024-12-31, labelled Documented 0.9, cited to AllAfrica metadata 15, unverifiable HTTP 403, whose description invoked a WHO validation workshop that no retrieved source supports). The MoHSS Executive Director's statement (Ben Nangombe, The Namibian 11 Mar 2025) is the only explicit absence claim covering 2015-2017, but it is demonstrably imprecise: a laboratory-confirmed V. cholerae case occurred in Katutura, Windhoek, 25-31 Jan 2018 (AI 6; JHU NA-KH; New Era 1 Feb 2018 Cholera outbreak confirmed). It is therefore accepted only as an inferred absence and only for the segment before the 2018 event: TR = 2018-01-21, the end of ISO week 3, so the event week (22-28 Jan 2018, private-doctor consultation 25 Jan) is left to AI 6. No contemporaneous 2015-2017 statement of absence was found: the New Era archive (WP API, Jun 2014-Jan 2018, 16 cholera-tagged items) reports no Namibian case; WHO WER annual reports 2016 and 2017 do not mention Namibia (non-reporting, not zero-reporting; metadata 146-147); WER 2015 PDF restricted (metadata 145). SURVEILLANCE operational: WHO Joint External Evaluation Dec 2016 (metadata 202) found a strong real-time surveillance system with IDSR syndromic surveillance for acute diarrhoea with dehydration and cholera laboratory testing; the single Jan 2018 case was detected, confirmed and published within a week, showing the system detects isolated cases. JHU national annual zeros 2015, 2016 (phantom) and 2017 agree. REGIONAL CROSS-CHECK: neighbour outbreaks in this period were far from the Namibian border - Zambia, Lusaka 2016 (>1000 cases) and Oct 2017-May 2018 (5905 suspected; Namibia banned Zambian food imports on 8 Jan 2018, New Era 10 Jan 2018); Angola 2016-2017 in Cabinda, Luanda and Zaire (252 cases, far north); Botswana none; a regionally moderate period with no outbreak in any border province. National total - no sub-national rows exist for this period. [AGENT 3 REVISION 2026-09-30] Agent 3 (batch 5) regional detail: New Era 10 Jan 2018 ('Namibia bans food imports from Zambia'): one Zambian case had been reported in Livingstone, about 200 km from the Namibian border, and MoHSS health officer L. Onesmus said 'apart from the one case reported in Livingstone, no other case has been reported in areas close to Namibia' (screening at Wenela border post from 8 Jan 2018). (reason: Agent 3 batch 5: regional context for early 2018) [AGENT 3 REVISION 2026-09-30] Agent 3 (batch 6): confidence lowered 0.6 -> 0.5. WHO AFRO IDS Quarterly Bulletin, 1st semester 2016 (metadata 216): Namibia is among 16 countries that 'didn't share data for the first semester of 2016', so WHO-facing surveillance was not transmitting Namibian IDSR data in this period - WHO silence 2015-2017 is non-reporting. The domestic system was operational (JEE Dec 2016, metadata 202) and the national press covered every other cholera event, so the inference of absence stands, at lower confidence. MoHSS repeated the imprecise decade claim in June 2025 (The Namibian 16 Jun 2025: 'Prior to this year, Namibia had enjoyed an entire decade free from cholera'). (reason: Agent 3 batch 6: WHO AFRO IDS 2016 shows Namibian IDSR data not shared with WHO)
retracted_reason: Agent 3 batch 6: superseded by a re-add of the same period (2015-01-01..2018-01-21) against a CONTEMPORANEOUS source - New Era 20 Sep 2018, Health Minister's National Assembly briefing: 'The last cholera outbreak experienced in Namibia was in 2013-2014' (metadata 217) - labelled Documented_Absence 0.5, instead of the 2025 retrospective MoHSS claim (metadata 197, Inferred 0.5).

source: WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record - Cholera in 1999 (WER 75(31):249-256)
processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 1999-01-01..1999-12-31. Source states: 'Cholera cases and deaths notified to WHO, 1999'. Evidence type: Inferred_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: operational. Namibia does not appear anywhere in the WER 1999 annual cholera notification table; the Africa block runs ...Malawi / Mali / Mauritania / Mozambique -> Niger / Nigeria... with no Namibia line. Namibia became independent on 1990-03-21 and joined WHO on 1990-04-23; cholera was one of three diseases subject to mandatory notification to WHO under the International Health Regulations (1969) throughout this period, so non-appearance in the annual notification table means no cholera cases were notified, not that no notification channel existed. Corroboration: (a) WHO Global Health Observatory annual cholera series (CHOLERA_0000000001) holds NO Namibia record before 2005 while neighbours are present from 1971 (Angola), 1973 (South Africa, Mozambique, Zimbabwe) and 1978 (Zambia); (b) the peer-reviewed report of Namibia's 2006-2007 outbreak states 'To date, there has been no published data of cholera occurring in Namibia' and 'this is the first published report of cholera from Namibia'. Evidence type: Inferred_Absence - inferred from absence of any notification in a mandatory WHO notification regime, not from an explicit WHO statement that Namibia reported zero. Caveat recorded in the WER 1990 issue itself: 'Evidence was again received of the presence of cholera in a number of other countries which failed to declare it' - underreporting cannot be excluded. Surveillance system status: operational (IHR(1969) cholera notification in force; Namibia a WHO Member State). National-level row; no sub-national rows exist for this period. [AGENT 3 REVISION 2026-09-30] Agent 3 (2026-09-30): this year is also covered by AI 174 (1990-03-21..2006-09-30, Documented_Absence 0.6), sourced to the Minister of Health's positive statement that cholera cases were 'reported for the first time in Namibia' in Nov/Dec 2006 (New Era 21 Feb 2007, metadata 211; repeated 21 Dec 2007, metadata 213). This row's own evidence (absence of a Namibia line in the WER annual table) remains Inferred; in the weekly builder AI 174's documented_zero supersedes it. (reason: Agent 3 T3: 1990-2005 upgrade cross-reference)
retracted_reason: Agent 4 batch 2: superseded by a re-add of the same period (1999-01-01..1999-12-31) against a STRONGER source - WHO Southern Block IDS Feedback Bulletin Issue 6 (Feb 2000, metadata 224), whose country table gives an explicit Namibia cholera 1999 = 0 cases / 0 deaths (and the Nov 1999 issue's Jan-Oct 1999 table shows Namibia 0 while marking non-reporters ND) - i.e. Documented_Absence instead of this row's Inferred_Absence from the Namibia line's absence in the WER 1999 annual table (metadata 28, carried into the new row's notes)

source: WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record - Cholera in 1977 (WER 53(17):117-118)
processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 1977-01-01..1977-12-31. Source states: 'Twelve countries in Africa reported a total of 8 388 cases as compared with 11 countries reporting 2 685 cases in 1976.'. Evidence type: Inferred_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: partial. Neither 'Namibia' nor 'South West Africa' appears anywhere in this year's WER cholera notification table. The table is headed 'Country/Area - Pays/Territoire' and does list non-sovereign territories in their own right (Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands, Guam, Hong Kong, Macao, Gaza), so a territory with cholera would have been expected to appear. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: in this period the territory was South West Africa under South African administration (independence 1990-03-21), it was not a WHO Member State, and any cases could in principle have been folded into the South Africa line or not notified at all - hence the reduced confidence (0.6) and surveillance status 'partial' rather than 'operational'. Supporting evidence: (a) WHO Global Health Observatory annual cholera series holds NO Namibia record before 2005, while Angola appears from 1971, South Africa/Mozambique/Zimbabwe from 1973 and Zambia from 1978; (b) WER 'Cholera in 1980' states 'South Africa, which had remained free of the disease since 1974, was once again infected in its northeastern region' and the South African 1980-1987 epidemic (25 251 bacteriologically proven cases) was confined to eastern Transvaal/KaNgwane, Limpopo, Mpumalanga and Natal/KwaZulu - rural areas with >600 mm mean annual rainfall - i.e. the opposite side of the subcontinent from arid South West Africa; (c) Namibia's FIRST-EVER appearance in a WER annual cholera table is 2006 ('Namibia/Namibie 185 5'), described there as spread 'across the Kunene river in the south to neighboring Namibia'; (d) the peer-reviewed report of that 2006-2007 outbreak states 'To date, there has been no published data of cholera occurring in Namibia'. Honesty caveat recorded by WHO itself: the WER annual reports of this era note that 'several additional countries could be considered also to be infected on the basis of earlier reports and information from other sources', so underreporting cannot be excluded. Evidence type: Inferred_Absence. National-level row; no sub-national rows exist for this period.
